summary.title: 10 usability heuristics every designer should know
summary.one_liner: Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics explained with everyday examples, giving designers a checklist for catching usability problems early.
keywords: don norman design of everyday things
how to design good error messages
takeaways: Nielsen's 10 heuristics remain useful as a checklist for early usability testing and new feature design.
Keep users informed with immediate feedback such as status indicators, loading spinners and state changes.
Use language and metaphors from the real world and follow platform conventions for consistency.
Prevent slips with constraints and confirmations, and prevent mistakes with clear communication and consistent design.
Write specific, polite error messages with next steps, and provide clear, well-structured onboarding and documentation.
summary.summary: The article revisits Jakob Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics, roughly 25 years after they were published, and argues they are still useful during early usability testing and as a design checklist. Each heuristic gets its own section with a definition, real-world examples from apps such as Apple's and Google's, and practical advice. Topics include system status feedback, real-world mental models, undo and emergency exits, consistency with platform guidelines, error prevention (slips vs. mistakes, drawing on Don Norman), recognition over recall, flexibility for novices and experts, minimalist design, error recovery messages, and help documentation. It is a conceptual overview with examples rather than a hands-on tutorial.
